terms.definition: An individual who registers and interacts with the COVE user management system. Users have roles (CUSTOMER or ADMIN), onboarding status, and account activation state.
The process by which a newly registered user is reviewed and approved or rejected by an administrator before gaining full system access.
The current state of a user's onboarding process. Valid values: pending_approval, approved, reject.
A short-lived JWT token (30 minutes validity) used to authenticate API requests. Stored in the database with expiration and revocation flags.
A long-lived JWT token (24 hours validity) used to obtain new access tokens without re-authentication. Stored in the database with expiration and revocation flags.
An audit log entry recording administrative actions performed on user accounts, including onboarding status changes, role updates, and account activation/deactivation.
A user's permission level within the system. Valid values: CUSTOMER (standard user) or ADMIN (administrative privileges).
Indicates whether a user account is currently active or deactivated. Active accounts can authenticate; deactivated accounts cannot.
The process by which a new user creates an account in the system, providing personal and company information. Registration triggers the onboarding workflow.
The process of verifying a user's identity using email and password credentials, resulting in the issuance of access and refresh tokens.
The process of invalidating access or refresh tokens, preventing their further use for authentication.
Automated email messages sent to users during onboarding workflow transitions (pending approval, approved, rejected).
Project performance metrics and RAG (Red-Amber-Green) status information retrieved from the external OneView API.

entities.name: User
entities.purpose: Represents an individual registered in the COVE system with authentication credentials, role-based permissions, and onboarding workflow state.

entities.name: AccessToken
entities.purpose: Represents a short-lived JWT token used for API authentication. Tracks token validity, expiration, and revocation status.

entities.name: RefreshToken
entities.purpose: Represents a long-lived JWT token used to obtain new access tokens without re-authentication. Tracks token validity, expiration, and revocation status.

entities.name: ActionHistory
entities.purpose: Audit log entry recording administrative actions performed on user accounts for compliance and traceability.
key_attributes: action (String: onboarding status | account status | role)
actionType (String: OnBoarding Status | Account Status | Role Status)

relationships.description: A User can have multiple AccessTokens over time. Each AccessToken belongs to exactly one User. Tokens are revoked and regenerated on each login.
A User can have multiple RefreshTokens over time. Each RefreshToken belongs to exactly one User. Tokens are revoked and regenerated on each login.

A User (as subject) can have multiple ActionHistory entries recording administrative actions performed on their account. ActionHistory is not directly linked via foreign key but associated by userEmail.
A User with ADMIN role can create multiple ActionHistory entries by performing administrative actions on other users. ActionHistory records the admin's email and name.
Users track who last updated their record via lastUpdatedBy field, creating an implicit relationship between users for audit purposes.

interfaces.description: Sends onboarding status notifications (pending, approved, rejected)

contexts.name: Authentication & Authorization
responsibilities: JWT access token generation and validation (30-minute validity)
JWT refresh token generation and validation (24-hour validity)

contexts.name: Audit & Compliance
responsibilities: Recording administrative actions on user accounts
Providing audit trail with admin attribution
Paginated audit log retrieval with filtering

contexts.name: External Integration

recommended_terms.usage: Prefer 'onboarding' over 'approval' or 'registration approval' to describe the user review process.
recommended_terms.rationale: Consistently used in code (OnboardingStatus, updateUserOnboardingStatus) and aligns with business process terminology.

recommended_terms.usage: Use 'access token' for short-lived authentication tokens; avoid 'auth token' or 'JWT token'.
recommended_terms.rationale: Distinguishes from refresh tokens and matches entity naming (AccessToken).

recommended_terms.usage: Use 'refresh token' for long-lived tokens used to obtain new access tokens.
recommended_terms.rationale: Matches entity naming (RefreshToken) and clearly differentiates from access tokens.

recommended_terms.usage: Use 'action history' for audit logs; avoid 'audit log' or 'admin log'.
recommended_terms.rationale: Matches entity naming (ActionHistory) and service naming (ActionHistoryService).

recommended_terms.usage: Use 'account status' to refer to active/deactivated state; avoid 'active status' or 'account state'.
recommended_terms.rationale: Matches constant naming (AccountStatus) and API endpoint naming.

naming_conflicts.description: The term 'Customer' is used as a role value (UserRole.Customer) but 'User' is the entity name (UserEntity). This creates ambiguity.
naming_conflicts.recommendation: Clarify that 'Customer' is a role type, not a separate entity. Use 'User with CUSTOMER role' in documentation.

naming_conflicts.description: Two similar-sounding status fields: onboardingStatus (pending_approval/approved/reject) and isActive (boolean account status).
naming_conflicts.recommendation: Clearly distinguish: 'Onboarding Status' governs approval workflow; 'Account Status' governs active/deactivated state post-approval.

naming_conflicts.description: ActionHistory entity has both 'action' (the status value) and 'actionType' (the category: OnBoarding Status, Account Status, Role Status).
naming_conflicts.recommendation: Rename 'action' to 'actionValue' or 'statusValue' and keep 'actionType' for category. This clarifies the distinction.
